pr_title: interrupt_controller: fixed IO APIC broadcasting issue (V2)
pr_body:
This is the updated version for this PR which was closed:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/22848

Currently IO APIC is working in physical destination mode, fixed delivery, and the destination fields in  IOREDTBL is fixed to 0xff, which seems a invalid configuration. By definition, in this setting, IO APIC interrupt can be delivered to one single local APIC whose LAPIC ID is 0xff.

This patchset is intended to fix the IO APIC delivery issue on SMP systems:

- change IO APIC from physical mode to logical destination mode so it's possible to deliver IO APIC interrupts to multiple local APICs.
- HPET timer interrupt needs to run in fixed delivery mode
- other device drivers are good to run in lowest priority mode

Tested:
1) sanitycheck -p qemu_x86
2) sanitycheck -p qemu_x86_64
3) Successfully ran samples/subsys/console/echo (test UART driver) and tests/kernel/queue (test timer interrupts) on these platforms:
- ACRN (x2apic)
- up_squared (both xapic and x2apic, SP and SMP)
- qemu_x86 (xapic)
- qemu_x86_64 (xapic, SP and SMP)

Can't test X2APIC with QEMU due to following warning:
qemu-system-x86_64: warning: TCG doesn't support requested feature: CPUID.01H:ECX.x2apic [bit 21]

fixes #21156

> This fails to build for `intel_s1000_crb`.

Fixed.

> We should avoid having the DTS interrupt encoding be zephyr specific. The concept of 'Fixed' and 'Lowest Level' seem to be encode how zephyr encodes irqs.

Within the current IRQ configuration architect, seems we have to encode the IRQ delivery mode in the .dts. Just need to find a best way to do that. Add a new cell to the interrupts property?

> Within the current IRQ configuration architect, seems we have to encode the IRQ delivery mode in the .dts. Just need to find a best way to do that. Add a new cell to the interrupts property?

what is the delivery mode mean?

> > Within the current IRQ configuration architect, seems we have to encode the IRQ delivery mode in the .dts. Just need to find a best way to do that. Add a new cell to the interrupts property?
> 
> what is the delivery mode mean?

Page 13 in:
https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/6.828/2014/readings/ia32/ioapic.pdf

Basically it's instructing IO APIC to deliver the external interrupt to all CPUs or just to one single CPU.
Yeah, an additional cell to encode this would make sense.

Would be good to update `dts/bindings/interrupt-controller/intel,ioapic.yaml` to provide a bit more detail about the encoding.  You can look at `dts/bindings/dma/st,stm32-dma.yaml ` for an example of describing encodes in description.

issue_context.title: Interrupts do not work on UP Squared board
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
`samples/boards/up_squared/gpio_counter` no longer works on UP Squared due to interrupts no longer being delivered.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. cd samples/boards/up_squared/gpio_counter/
2. mkdir build; cd build
3. cmake -DBOARD=up_squared
4. make
5. Set BIOS configurations described inside `src/main.c`.
6. Boot the Zephyr image according to documentation.
7. Observe the counter would not increment when inputs are pulsed on HAT pin 16.

**Expected behavior**
The counter would increment, and reflected on the 4-bit output of pin35/37/38/40.

**Impact**
- Broken board support.
- Blocking verification of GPIO API changes and app updates.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK 0.10.3
 - Commit: 58e2057aaf9af4d299814f4aece585e287587162
comments: @dcpleung do you know if anyone is looking at this? Should it be reassigned to someone else?

I have been looking at this on-and-off. The problems are lack of documentation on IO-APIC, and QEMU having the 0xFF broadcast which does not seem to be the case for actual hardware. One of the solution is to use logical destination, which works on UP^2 but fails QEMU. So more investigation is needed.
Reopening this. I had to revert @ZideChen0 change #22848 as it was causing timeouts when running tests on qemu_x86_64. Needs further analysis.

review_comments: Why do you need to encode this explicitly?

Take an UART interrupt as example, all the way from the generated code (e.g. uart_ns16650_port_0.h) to the ioapic driver:

irq_connect_dynamic() -> arch_irq_connect_dynamic() ->z_irq_controller_irq_config() ->z_ioapic_irq_set().

The only way to config different interrupt with different delivery mode (fixed vs lowest priority) is through the irq_flags that is generated from the .dts.

Thus, the easiest approach available is to change these macros as I did in this patch. Other alternatives that I can think of:

Don't change the name of IRQ_TYPE_xxx macros, but silently change it's content:
 #define IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_LOW (IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL | IRQ_TYPE_LOW|IRQ_DELIVERY_LOWEST) 

Add one more cell to the interrupts property. But this seems a big change. For example:
 interrupts = <4 IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_RISING IRQ_DELIVERY_LOWEST_PRIO 3>
